topic: Migrate from Claude Opus 4.8 to Claude Fable 5: What Changes (2026)

key_points: Official migration guidance says to update the model ID from claude-opus-4-8 to claude-fable-5.
Fable 5 runs with adaptive thinking by default; disabling thinking returns an error.
Developers must revisit max_tokens because thinking plus visible response share the output budget.
Organizations with zero data retention must confirm eligibility because Fable 5 requires 30-day retention.
Use high effort as the default on Fable 5 and reserve xhigh for the most capability-sensitive workloads.
Fable 5 is positioned as Anthropic's most capable widely released model for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work.
The API model ID is claude-fable-5; it has a 1M token context window and up to 128k output tokens.
Pricing is listed at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.
Fable 5 refusals return stop_reason: refusal as a successful HTTP 200 response, so applications must check stop reasons.
Fallbacks can be server-side, SDK middleware-based, or manually implemented.
Anthropic frames Fable 5 as the general-release version of Mythos-class capability, with added safety classifiers.
Launch examples emphasize fewer turns, long-horizon reasoning, coding workflows, spreadsheet analysis, physics research, and vibe-coding.
Anthropic acknowledges safeguards are intentionally cautious and may produce false positives.
High-risk cybersecurity and biology capabilities are the central reason for the added classifier layer.
The piece gives writers vendor positioning and quotes, but should be balanced with independent evaluation and production caveats.
Compares Fable 5 and Opus 4.8 across benchmarks, price, context, safeguards, data retention, and migration steps.
Highlights headline benchmark gaps: 80.3% vs 69.2% on SWE-bench Pro and 29.3% vs 13.4% on FrontierCode Diamond.
Frames the 2x price difference as a routing decision rather than a default upgrade.
Calls out 30-day retention as a hidden enterprise switching cost.
Recommends benchmarking real tasks, adding refusal handling, retuning effort, and routing only the failure-prone tail to Fable 5.
Argues Opus 4.8 may remain the better value for many agent fleets despite Fable 5's frontier positioning.
Reports an internal evaluation of roughly 1,000 shared scenarios.
Emphasizes that supplied skills/context improved both models by about 17 points, more than the model upgrade in that test.
Useful counter-position: migration success depends on harness quality, prompts, skills, and evaluation data, not model name alone.
Supports a nuanced article angle around evaluation-first migration instead of blanket replacement.

stats.fact: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 became available on June 9, 2026; Fable 5 is generally available on Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.
Claude Fable 5 uses the API model ID claude-fable-5, supports a 1M token context window by default, and supports up to 128k output tokens per request.
Claude Fable 5 pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, compared with Opus 4.8 comparisons commonly listing $5/$25 per million input/output tokens.
Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are covered models with 30-day data retention and are not available under zero data retention.
When Claude Fable 5 declines a request, the Messages API returns stop_reason: refusal as HTTP 200 rather than an HTTP error.
Anthropic's migration guide says requests without a thinking field run with adaptive thinking on claude-fable-5, and max_tokens remains a hard cap across thinking plus response text.

Anthropic recommends high effort as the default for most Fable 5 tasks and reserving xhigh for the most capability-sensitive workloads, whereas Opus 4.8 coding and high-autonomy work often used xhigh.
Coursiv reports Anthropic-published benchmark deltas of 80.3% vs 69.2% on SWE-bench Pro and 29.3% vs 13.4% on FrontierCode Diamond for Fable 5 vs Opus 4.8.
Anthropic says Fable 5's safeguards are intentionally cautious and may trigger benign false positives while the system is refined.
Tessl's evaluation angle found supplied skills/context moved both models by about 17 points, suggesting migration quality depends heavily on prompts, skills, and eval harnesses.

angles: Treat Fable 5 as a production migration, not a model-name swap: thinking behavior, max_tokens, refusals, fallback, retention, and billing all need code or policy review.
The winning 2026 strategy is routing: keep Opus 4.8 for routine, latency-sensitive, high-volume, ZDR-bound, or safeguarded-domain traffic; send long-horizon, failure-prone work to Fable 5.
Benchmark vendor claims against your own completion rate, total turns, tool calls, human edits, latency, and cost per successful task.
The hidden enterprise blocker is data retention: Fable 5's 30-day retention can be more important than benchmark gains for regulated or confidential workloads.
Refusal handling is a compatibility change: a 200 response can still mean the Fable path did not complete the request.
Prompt and context quality may matter as much as the upgrade; skill files, evaluation harnesses, and task decomposition can preserve Opus 4.8 value.
Use Fable 5's higher capability where failures compound across many steps, such as multi-repo migrations, long-context audits, and complex agent workflows.
Cost should be measured per completed task, not per token, because Fable 5 may use fewer turns on hard jobs but remains wasteful on simple jobs.
